original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Can source-bound variable-rank diagonal batching bring the selected complex profile above the kappa=0.1 planning target under an explicit six-unpaid coverage hypothesis, and how much interface cost can it tolerate?
scope_change_reason: The donor-set target kappa>0.1 is much larger than the coverage card's two-unpaid first experiment. The source-bound batching screen combines a changed rank profile with the minimum tested coverage value that crosses a=1/9; it deliberately stops before constructing that six-unpaid endpoint or a physical batch.
bottleneck_link: The selected profile spends most mass in ranks 1 through 5. The source schedule can fuse 5,520 of 5,522 climb-rank units into summed-rank children, but the exact target moment crosses one only at six unpaid coordinates and leaves at most six rank-one-equivalent units per call for all interface work.
stop_rule: Do not continue the fixed PR2757 aligned six-mode family: two Python 3.12 implementations replayed here report a scoped floor C >= 297 against the necessary C <= 296 gate. Continue only with a named changed cover or mode assignment. For that changed route, before broad search or fusion work, price one exact dirty-input endpoint and one complete batch; stop if endpoint, gathering, frames, delivery and restoration exceed the six rank-one-equivalent units per call.
evidence: The pinned forward and backward selected programs give the same 256-batch profile; the independent local checker accepts the within-window reorder; the heterogeneous direct-sum identity is checked; exact outward-rational moments pass a=1/9 only at the hypothetical u=6 (with centre mass 64), with six extra rank-one-equivalent units passing and seven failing. Post-refresh context: current main contains a scoped P112 six-mode package reporting cost at least 297 for the fixed aligned PR2757 family, above the necessary 296 gate.
